title: Prove sharp fixed-support unary-query bounds with restored dirty banks
body:
## Summary

- Prove a sharp `2n` query bound for applying a fixed carrier squared to `n` independent data banks while restoring any finite number of arbitrary dirty helper banks. Two queries per output attain the bound.
- Allow free invertible bank mixing over the internal-swap algebra for the balanced order-four carrier. A separate quartic theorem proves the same bound with scalar bank mixing.
- Keep the paid-scan counterexample alongside the theorem: additional ADDRESS-valued operations can produce two full chirps with zero native queries, but require `6mf` complete ADD scans plus paid swaps, signs and addressing.

Package and detailed proofs: [fixed-support-unary-query-bounds](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/tree/9124007ea9029a9a3b88898bb4c350ddb27ffa58/research/fixed-support-unary-query-bounds).

## Scope and limits

The main theorem is over a characteristic-zero field containing `i`, with fixed support, balanced `N²=-I`, carrier `A=(N⊗I)S`, one-bank `A` or `A⁻¹` queries and exact restoration of every extra bank. The quartic companion requires all four eigencharacters of `z⁴+1` and scalar bridges; it does not inherit the larger swap-algebra alphabet.

The quantified lower bounds are written proofs. Finite exact witnesses verify actual constituents and noncommuting word identities, including all 32 sign choices of one five-query word and meaningful order/phase/omission controls. They are not exhaustive word searches or formal-kernel proofs. Changing supports, permitted operators or restoration changes the premises. Native pricing and physical implementation remain separate; no new kappa, selected-frontier improvement or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Test plan

Publication head: `9124007ea9029a9a3b88898bb4c350ddb27ffa58`.

- [x] `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fixed-support-unary-query-bounds` — registered normal and optimized replay, exact Gaussian/full group-algebra identities, quartic and scan fixtures, defect controls.
- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/fixed-support-unary-query-bounds --check-source-history` — committed bytes and source history.
- [x] Authenticated prior Git-free export replay and separate AI proof review; these are preserved evidence, not independent human or formal-kernel review.
- [x] Automatic [Registered research packages CI](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39232467343) passed at this exact head, including registered replay and unchanged committed inputs.

The package uses Python 3.12 and the standard library. Replay requires no private checker, Git checkout or external local research directory.

## Sources and credit

Scientific base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; exact context and local predecessor lineage are in `SOURCES.json`, `LOCAL-PROVENANCE.json` and `predecessor/`. The original fixed-support proof, quartic companion and scan construction are retained with a separate independent AI derivation and portable replay. The causal factorization, image/row-space and character-rank methods credit eumemic's [retained PR288 source](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90/research/abelian-cayley-metric-scope/sources/pr288-README.md) and Ali Romman's [PR468](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/07a78bf335b0b5039a1fecd7cd74a0fe1d1605ea/research/bit-three-register-lower-bound/README.md). Jose Manuel's [PR2108](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b25eb9b6a95d8b644c582a5c0d8229bc2ffc3eb7/research/two-register-three-mix/README.md) is related two-register, three-mixing-block work. Here the distinct claim is this fixed carrier's sharp bound with arbitrary finite restored dirt and unrestricted-length swap-algebra bridges, plus the scalar quartic companion. No claim of an entirely new proof method or exhaustive novelty is made.

Apache-2.0. Prepared by Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. This PR is the canonical public record for this bounded contribution.
